## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #495 implements issue #452 by publishing one finalized orchestration note at terminal states. It tags human requesters, reuses live progress comments, and updates existing marker-based notes instead of posting duplicates. Successful PR outcomes also collapse older trusted review, rubrics, fix, and handoff artifacts. The intended result is a concise terminal summary that preserves actionable context whenever orchestration blocks or fails.

## Review

The happy path is well-scoped and thoroughly tested, but the current implementation can hide required context and gives the planner broader authorization than its decision role requires. Reviewers disagreed about the cleanup and permission designs; inspection of the current head and issue #452 confirms the blocking cases below.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Blocked planner outcomes trigger success cleanup | BLOCKING | The cleanup guard uses only the source `review`/`SHIP` tuple, so a subsequent planner `blocked` decision still minimizes actionable artifacts. This directly violates issue #452’s blocked/clarification requirement. |
| Planner receives a PR-write credential | BLOCKING | The workflow grants job-wide `pull-requests: write` and passes the resolved token into the approve-all planner before deterministic validation, allowing the decision gate to perform PR mutations directly. |
| Finalized note can minimize itself | WARNING | Cleanup runs after publication, and broad legacy matchers can select the new final note when its free-form summary contains a recognized heading such as `## Rubrics Review`. |
| Legacy stop marker can duplicate final notes | WARNING | Lookup recognizes only `sepo-agent-orchestrate-final`, so an upgraded rerun can leave a trusted `sepo-agent-orchestrate-stop` note visible and create another finalized note. |
| Progress comment IDs obscure provenance | INFO | A module-level environment-derived `progressCommentId` shadows a fetched-comment-derived local variable with different trust semantics, creating a future maintenance footgun. |

## Progress

- Exact head `dd129eb3` passes the TypeScript build, 70 handoff tests, 92 workflow checks, five documentation checks, and `git diff --check`.
- Human-requester filtering, marker upsert, progress-note reuse, merge-failure fallback, trusted-only cleanup, documentation, and release-note discipline are implemented correctly.
- The existing rubrics-review comment already covers the credential boundary and legacy-marker migration, so those were not duplicated inline.
- Two inline comments were posted for the newly confirmed cleanup bugs: [blocked-state cleanup](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495#discussion_r3753886864) and [final-note self-minimization](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495#discussion_r3753886855).
- No prior inline comments or review threads required replies, minimization, or resolution.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Blocked planner outcomes trigger success cleanup</summary>

**Cause:** [`collapseSuccessfulPrArtifacts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/dd129eb3d245c859aaf49facae5d3bc11dcea280/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1234) derives eligibility solely from `SOURCE_ACTION` and `SOURCE_CONCLUSION`; it never considers `decision.plannerDecisionKind === "blocked"`.

**Candidate solutions:** Pass the terminal decision into the cleanup predicate, require a genuinely successful non-blocked outcome, and add a regression for `review`/`SHIP` followed by planner `blocked`.

**Comments:** One reviewer considered the success gate correct, but that assessment did not account for the later planner decision. Issue #452 explicitly requires blocked and clarification paths to retain their artifacts.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Planner receives a PR-write credential</summary>

**Cause:** [`agent-orchestrator.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/dd129eb3d245c859aaf49facae5d3bc11dcea280/.github/workflows/agent-orchestrator.yml#L79) grants the whole job PR-write access and passes its resolved token to the approve-all planner before the deterministic handoff step.

**Candidate solutions:** Keep the planner on a read-scoped credential/job, isolate finalized-comment and minimization writes in a deterministic write-scoped step or job, and add a workflow test protecting that boundary.

**Comments:** One reviewer considered the permission necessary and consistent with review workflows. The contrary review is more persuasive because this repository already documents the read-agent/write-resolver separation for self-approval, and the planner only needs to choose an action.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Finalized note can minimize itself</summary>

**Cause:** The [cleanup call](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/dd129eb3d245c859aaf49facae5d3bc11dcea280/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1295) runs after publication, while legacy matchers scan every same-agent PR comment without excluding `ORCHESTRATE_FINAL_MARKER`.

**Candidate solutions:** Explicitly exclude finalized-note IDs or marker-bearing bodies from every cleanup pass, or safely perform cleanup before publication. Cover a final `user_message` containing a legacy review signature.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Legacy stop marker can duplicate final notes</summary>

**Cause:** [`findTrustedOrchestrateFinalComment`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/dd129eb3d245c859aaf49facae5d3bc11dcea280/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1221) searches only for the new marker.

**Candidate solutions:** Recognize both trusted legacy and current markers, update the newest applicable comment in place, and rewrite migrated notes with the current marker. Add an upgraded-rerun regression.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Progress comment IDs obscure provenance</summary>

**Cause:** The environment-derived module constant and fetched-comment-derived local variable share the name `progressCommentId`.

**Candidate solutions:** Rename the module value to `envProgressCommentId` or `dispatchedProgressCommentId`.

**Comments:** This does not change current behavior and is intentionally excluded from required automation action items.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: The confirmed cleanup bugs, credential boundary, and marker migration all have concrete branch changes and regression coverage suitable for an automated fix pass.

## Final Verdict

`NEEDS_REWORK`

- [ ] Exclude the newly finalized note from all artifact-cleanup matchers and add a self-minimization regression.

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue

[PR #495](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495) implements [issue #452](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/452) by publishing or updating one finalized orchestration note at terminal states. It includes the cumulative planner summary, mentions human requesters, migrates legacy markers, and attempts to reuse live progress comments. Successful PR outcomes also collapse older trusted review, rubrics, fix, and handoff artifacts while preserving blocked or clarification context. The current head separates the read-only planner from a deterministic write-capable resolver.

## Review

The four earlier authorization, blocked-cleanup, self-minimization, and legacy-marker findings are fixed, but two blocking lifecycle defects and one broken documented progress path remain. Reviewers disagreed about `always()` and progress severity; current GitHub semantics confirm the cancellation defect, while the working marker fallback justifies classifying progress as WARNING rather than another blocker.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Cancellation can enter the write-capable resolver | BLOCKING | The resolver uses `always()`, so cancellation after the job starts does not stop it; it can retain write credentials and continue commenting, minimizing, or dispatching. |
| Planner failures are treated as successful | BLOCKING | Missing or malformed planner output produces an invalid-planner stop, but `review`/`SHIP` is still rendered as successful and triggers cleanup of prior actionable artifacts. |
| Configured planner progress cannot publish | WARNING | The reporter receives the planner’s read-only token, cannot create its advertised progress comment, and hides the failure before falling back to a separate final note. |

## Progress

- Head `b41afca2` fixes the four earlier findings: planner authorization isolation, blocked-state retention, final-note cleanup exclusion, and legacy-marker migration.
- Reviewer verification and the hosted `Test Scripts` check are green, including the build, 73 handoff tests, cleanup/minimizer suites, 93 workflow checks, five documentation checks, and `git diff --check`.
- Posted inline feedback for [planner-failure classification](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495#discussion_r3754136406) and [cancellation handling](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495#discussion_r3754136408). The existing [rubrics review](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495#issuecomment-5246988371) already covers the progress-path defect, so it was not duplicated inline.
- Resolved the fixed same-agent [self-minimization](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495#discussion_r3753886855) and [blocked-cleanup](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/495#discussion_r3753886864) threads. No comments were replied to or minimized.
- Optional naming and additional self-approval/self-merge coverage notes remain INFO-only and are excluded from required work.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Cancellation can enter the write-capable resolver</summary>

**Cause:** [`decide-and-dispatch`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b41afca252e85b25292b4d6ab85f1730db3ad065/.github/workflows/agent-orchestrator.yml#L210-L219) combines `always()` with actions, issues, and pull-request write permissions. GitHub documents that a running job whose condition remains true under `always()` is not canceled during workflow cancellation ([workflow cancellation reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-cancellation)).

**Candidate solutions:** Use a cancellation-aware condition such as `${{ !cancelled() && vars.AGENT_ENABLED != 'false' }}`, preserving fallback after ordinary planner failure or skipping, and add a workflow assertion.

**Comments:** One reviewer considered `always()` intentional for planner failure handling, but that does not justify continuing write-capable automation after explicit cancellation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Planner failures are treated as successful</summary>

**Cause:** [`readPlannerDecision()`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b41afca252e85b25292b4d6ab85f1730db3ad065/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L900-L907) returns `null` for missing or malformed output, while [`isSuccessfulPrTerminalState()`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b41afca252e85b25292b4d6ab85f1730db3ad065/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1104-L1112) considers only the source action/conclusion. Consequently the invalid-planner stop receives success wording and passes [artifact cleanup](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b41afca252e85b25292b4d6ab85f1730db3ad065/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1235-L1243).

**Candidate solutions:** Derive success from both the source tuple and a validated terminal decision; in agent mode, missing or invalid planner output must retain prior artifacts and use failure-oriented wording. Add missing and malformed response regressions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Configured planner progress cannot publish</summary>

**Cause:** The planner is correctly read-only, but its [progress reporter](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b41afca252e85b25292b4d6ab85f1730db3ad065/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L409-L440) uses that same token to create comments, which requires Issues or Pull Requests write permission ([GitHub API permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments#create-an-issue-comment)).
